lines.meet: Hello, I'm Clara. I study tree rings, or I did, and now I heal people because the tree seems to like me.
lines.meet_neighbour: You're at Mossroof too, aren't you? I'm the one sitting on the moss with a notebook, muttering.
lines.ask_home: Can I ask where you grew up? I'm curious about everybody, sorry.
lines.ask_work: How did you spend your days at home? I'm nosy about it with everyone.
lines.answer_home: Freiburg, in the south of Germany, right at the edge of the Black Forest. Cobbled streets, little streams in the gutters, and pine everywhere.
lines.answer_work: Dendrochronology, which is a long word for reading tree rings. I had a tiny lab and a wall of cores in straws.
lines.chat_food: Black Forest cake from the bakery on my street, on a Sunday, with far too much cream. I'm not ashamed.
lines.chat_sleep: I fall asleep reading, every night, and wake up with a book on my face and the lamp still on.
lines.chat_missing: Cycling up into the Black Forest on a Saturday morning, with the mist still in the valleys and a thermos in the basket.
lines.chat_here: This tree has no rings anywhere I've cored it, and it's driving me completely mad. I'll work it out, though.
lines.tease_quiet: You'd be lovely in a lab, {name}. Quiet, careful, and you'd never knock over my samples.
lines.tease_talker: I didn't think anyone could out-talk me, {name}, and yet here you are.
lines.tease_careful: You'd make an excellent scientist, {name}. You test everything before you trust it, and I adore that.
lines.tease_bold: You'd climb a tree without looking at the branches first, {name}. I'd have to take notes on the fall.
lines.tease_any: I'd love to know what goes on in your head, {name}, though I suspect I'd need a whole notebook.
lines.tease_back: Oh, that's fair, {name}, you've got me exactly.
lines.take_it_kindly: Oh, that's fair, {name}, I'll admit it. My mother says the same.
lines.bristle: That one hurts, {name}, so please don't. I missed my grandmother's funeral, and I'm not proud of it.
lines.needle_quiet: If something's wrong, please say it out loud. I can't fix what I don't know about.
lines.needle_talker: Could we have a little quiet? I'm trying to listen for what's coming.
lines.needle_careful: At some point we have enough evidence and we just have to act on it.
lines.needle_bold: You rush in without looking, and I'm the one who has to put you back together afterwards.
lines.needle_any: You never stop to check, and one day that's going to cost somebody dearly.
lines.bite_back: I've healed all of you through every fight we've had. Please don't tell me I'm not helping.
lines.hurt: That hurt, honestly it did. I'm going to go and sit with my notes for a while.
lines.laugh_off: My doctoral committee said far worse about my methodology. I survived them, and I'll survive you.
lines.apologise: Sorry, I put that badly. I was frustrated, and I took it out on you.
lines.double_down: I'm afraid I meant it. The evidence was right there, and somebody needed to say so.
lines.confide: {name}, I missed my grandmother's funeral for a field season. She used to bring me pinecones and ask how old they were.
lines.listen: Tell me properly, {name}, all of it. I'm here, and I'm listening.
lines.look_out: Stay by me, {name}, so I can reach you quickly.
lines.accept: We'll try your way, {name}, and I'll watch closely.
lines.deflect: It's only a scrape, {name}. See to somebody who needs it more.
lines.check_in: Hold still a moment, {name}. I need to see that, and it won't hurt for long.
lines.blame: Somebody went ahead without checking, and I couldn't get to everyone in time.
lines.thank: You kept me safe there, and I noticed. Thank you, really.
lines.brush_off: Please, it was nothing. Keeping people well is the job.
lines.worry: Stay with me, {name}, keep breathing. I've got you, I'm right here.
lines.handed_down: This really belongs with you. Please take it back.
lines.hand_fine: Please, take it, honestly I don't mind. I spent most of my life in wellies and a fleece.
lines.hand_sulk: So I wasn't asked. That's fine, really, I'm not upset.
lines.turn_friendly: I'd trust your measurements, {name}, and from me that's a very high compliment.
lines.turn_friends: You're one of my favourite people on any world, {name}, and I've thought about it carefully.
lines.turn_grating: I don't think we suit each other, you and I. We can still do good work together.
lines.turn_rivals: You'll still get healed, of course you will. I just won't chat while I do it.
lines.make_up: Can we start again, {name}? I'd really like to.
lines.defend: That's unfair, please stop. {name} did everything right, and I saw it.
lines.friend_left: Mossroof is too quiet without {name}. I keep saving things to tell them.
lines.friend_back: {name}, oh, I'm so glad you're here again! I've got about forty things to tell you.
lines.common_growing: You've grown things, I can tell. People who garden always look at the soil before the sky.
lines.common_wild: You know the wild places, don't you? You walk through a forest like you're visiting someone's house.
